transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today?

Hi… thank you for seeing me. I guess I’m here because I’ve just been really tired all the time. I try not to make a big deal out of it, but by midmorning at work—even if I’m just reviewing claim files or walking a junior adjuster through something—I feel like my body and my brain are already running on empty. Does that make sense?
Have you noticed your mood being down or feeling hopeless, especially along with this fatigue?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I wouldn’t want to make it sound dramatic, but most days it’s like there’s this gray film over everything. Even when my husband is being sweet, or we’re cooking with the family and it should feel nice, I’m there and I’m doing it… I just don’t really feel the enjoyment the way I used to. Does that make sense?
Do these feelings of fatigue and the gray film over things happen most days, and do they tend to last throughout the day, or do they come and go?

Most days, yes… I mean, I don’t want to overstate it, but it’s there a lot. That gray feeling kind of follows me through the day. I can still do what I need to do, and if my husband is kind or we’re cooking with family, I’m present and going through the motions… I just don’t really feel the enjoyment like I used to. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
So you mentioned the fatigue and that gray feeling are there a lot—can you clarify if those feelings happen nearly every day, and if so, do they last for most of the day?

Yes… I think nearly every day would be fair to say. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, because I do still get things done, but most days it’s like that gray film is just there over everything. Even if my husband is being kind, or we’re cooking with the family, I’m going through the motions more than really enjoying it. It’s there for most of the day, I’d say.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy, such as hobbies, time with family, or other things you’ve done in the past?

Yes… I guess I have noticed that. I don’t want to make it sound like I don’t care about anything, because I do. But even when my husband is being kind, or when we’re cooking with the family and it should feel warm and nice, I’m sort of just… there. Going through the motions. Most days it feels like there’s this gray film over everything, and I don’t really get the enjoyment from things the way I used to. Is that what you mean?
Have you felt this way for a long time, like at least a couple of years, or is this something that started more recently, within the past few months?

It’s been longer than just a few months… I think about three years, maybe a little over. Around three years and three months, if I’m remembering right. It started after I was moved into that higher-responsibility role at work, mentoring other adjusters and helping oversee the new workflow systems. I don’t want to blame everything on the job, but that’s when I really noticed it settling in.
Have you had a depressed mood most of the day, more days than not, for at least two years?

Yes… I think so. I don’t want to overstate it, but most days I do feel like there’s this gray film over everything. Even when things are objectively good—like my husband being kind, or us cooking with the family—I can go through the motions, but I’m not really feeling the enjoyment the way I used to. So… yes, more days than not, and most of the day, I’d say.
Have you noticed that you get tired more easily or that you have a loss of energy almost every day, even if you haven’t done much physically or mentally?

Yes… I think that’s actually one of the main reasons I came in. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but I’m tired all the time. Like, by midmorning at work, after I’ve only been reviewing files or walking a junior adjuster through a claim, it already feels like my body and my brain are running on empty. Even if I haven’t done anything especially hard physically. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight over the same time period—like eating more or less than usual or gaining or losing weight without trying?

I don’t think there’s been a big change there, honestly. My appetite is… mostly about the same, I guess. I haven’t noticed my weight moving much either, not in any way I was worried about. If anything, it just varies day to day like normal, but nothing I’d point to as a real change.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep lately, like trouble falling asleep, waking up during the night, or waking up earlier than usual and not being able to go back to sleep?

I’m not sure I’d say there’s been a real change… I mean, I have the occasional night where I don’t sleep great, but I think that’s pretty normal, right? I haven’t noticed a clear pattern like consistently waking up early or being up all night. Nothing that’s stood out to me as a major sleep problem.
Have you noticed any trouble concentrating, making decisions, or thinking clearly most days?

A little, yes… I mean, I’m still getting my work done, mostly, so I don’t want to overstate it. But I have noticed I’m missing details in audits that I normally would catch, and it’s taking me longer to feel comfortable signing off on files. I keep double-checking myself.

And outside of work, I guess I’ve kind of pulled back from things like painting, hiking, and volunteering. Not because I don’t care about them, just… by the time I get through the week, I don’t have much left. Does that count as trouble concentrating, or is that more just being worn out?
Have you lost interest in doing things you used to enjoy, like painting, hiking, or volunteering, even when you have the time to do them?

Yes… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, because I still do things when I’m supposed to, and if my husband is being kind or we’re cooking with the family, I can smile and participate.

But most days it’s like there’s this gray film over everything. I go through the motions, and I know these are things I used to enjoy, but I don’t really feel the enjoyment the same way. Is that what you mean?
Have you noticed that your movements or speech have slowed down, or that you feel more restless or agitated than usual, almost every day?

I don’t think so… at least, no one’s told me I’m talking slower or moving differently. I might feel a little tense sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’m pacing or agitated almost every day.

Maybe I’m not the best judge of it, though. Is that the kind of thing other people usually notice first?
Have you noticed that you've been harder on yourself or more critical than usual, or had feelings of guilt or worthlessness almost every day?

I’m not sure I’d say “worthless,” exactly. That sounds… stronger than what I’d want to claim.

I do second-guess myself, and I can be pretty hard on myself when I don’t handle something the way I think I should. But I’ve kind of always had high standards, so I don’t know if that counts as more than usual. I don’t walk around every day thinking I’m a terrible person or anything.

Maybe it’s more like… I feel disappointed in myself sometimes. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?
